NutriFresh Foods Inc. - Q3 2023 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NutriFresh Foods Inc. Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Thompson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NutriFresh Foods Inc.'s Q3 2023 results. Joining me on the call are Mike Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Growth Officer; and Tom Bradley, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Mike Rivera.

Mike Rivera (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2023. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on eight key areas: E-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue, Impact of new product innovations and launches, Revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance, Impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue, EBITDA margin performance and key factors, Organic revenue growth: overall and by region, Performance in key channels: retail, foodservice, convenience, and Performance of key brands and product categories.

First, regarding E-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue: Our e-commerce channel accelerated sharply, reaching 18% penetration of net revenues, up significantly year-over-year.

Second, concerning Impact of new product innovations and launches: New products drove 18% of segment sales with 32% growth, boosting margins through premiumization.

Third, in terms of Revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance: We're reaffirming at the top end with an upward nudge to EPS, reflecting momentum.

Fourth, looking at Impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue: FX posed a 320 basis point headwind to reported growth, but constant currency was robust.

Fifth, reviewing EBITDA margin performance and key factors: Margins expanded 140 basis points to 17.8%, driven by pricing and efficiencies.

Sixth, analyzing Organic revenue growth: overall and by region: We achieved 6.8% organic growth, balanced across regions.

Seventh, examining Performance in key channels: retail, foodservice, convenience: Channels grew 8.2% organically, led by foodservice and convenience.

Eighth, considering Performance of key brands and product categories: Our core brands delivered 8.2% organic growth, with beverages leading at 11.7%.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins to provide more detail on our financial results.

Sarah Jenkins (CFO):
Thank you, Mike. As Mike mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 2023. Net sales were $3.2 billion, representing an 8% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 38.5%, impacted by favorable product mix and productivity gains from supply chain initiatives. Operating income was $480 million, and earnings per share were $1.15. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.8 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for organic net sales growth of 5% to 6%, adjusted EBITDA margins of 19% to 19.5%, and adjusted diluted EPS of $4.55 to $4.70.

To give more color on the eight key areas Mike highlighted, let me start with e-commerce sales growth and their contribution to total revenue. This channel continues to be a standout driver of our top-line growth amid a challenging macroeconomic environment for the Food & Beverage sector. With consumers increasingly prioritizing convenience, health-focused products, and seamless digital experiences—especially in the wake of persistent inflation pressures on brick-and-mortar grocery shopping—our e-commerce sales have accelerated and are reshaping our revenue mix in a structurally positive way.

In Q3, e-commerce sales reached $285 million, marking a robust 48% year-over-year increase and a 12% sequential improvement from Q2. This brought our e-commerce penetration to 18% of total net revenues—up from 12% in the prior-year period and 16% in Q2—representing the highest quarterly contribution in our company's history. For context, full-year 2023 e-commerce sales are tracking at approximately $1.05 billion, putting us on pace for 52% year-over-year growth and a full-year revenue mix of around 17%. This outpaces the broader industry benchmark; according to NielsenIQ data, the U.S. F&B e-commerce category grew 32% year-over-year in Q3, while our direct-to-consumer and marketplace channels are lapping that by a wide margin.

Breaking it down by sub-channel, our DTC platform—powered by our proprietary NutriFresh Direct app and website—accounted for 62% of e-commerce sales at $177 million, up 55% year-over-year. Average order value here expanded 14% to $68, driven by personalized bundling algorithms that promote our high-margin functional beverage line, like our zero-sugar electrolyte drinks, alongside bestsellers such as Organic Harvest snack bars. Subscription revenue within DTC now comprises 28% of this sub-channel, growing 72% year-over-year, mimicking the success of peers like Chobani with its subscription yogurt deliveries or Vital Proteins' collagen model. Our customer retention rate stands at 68% for subscribers, with lifetime value up 22% to $450 per customer.

Marketplace sales via partners like Amazon Fresh, Instacart, Walmart+, and DoorDash contributed the remaining 38% or $108 million, surging 38% year-over-year. This channel benefited from expanded listings—we've now launched 85 SKUs across these platforms, including our new plant-based ready-to-eat meal kits that align with the 25% year-over-year category growth in meal solutions per IRI data. Sponsored product ads on Amazon yielded a 4.2x return on ad spend, helping us capture 1.8% share in the $15 billion online healthy snacks segment.

Regionally, North America remains our powerhouse, delivering 82% of e-commerce revenues at $234 million, up 51% year-over-year, fueled by high smartphone penetration and same-day delivery infrastructure. In EMEA, we're at $32 million, up 29% year-over-year, tempered by stricter food labeling regs under the EU Green Deal, but we've mitigated this through localized listings on Ocado and Just Eat Takeaway, with average order value up 9% to €52 on premium kombucha SKUs. APAC is the fastest grower at 65% year-over-year to $19 million, led by Tmall and Shopee partnerships in China and Southeast Asia, where urban millennials are snapping up our low-cal protein shakes—basket sizes here average 15% higher than NA due to multi-pack promotions.

From a technical standpoint, our growth isn't accidental—it's the result of $45 million invested over the past 18 months in digital infrastructure. We've migrated to a composable commerce stack using Shopify Plus for DTC, integrated with Snowflake for real-time inventory sync and Adobe Experience Manager for AI-powered recommendations, boosting conversion rates by 23% to 4.1%. Our omnichannel fulfillment network, now with five micro-fulfillment centers co-located near urban hubs like those pioneered by Kroger's Ocado partnership, has slashed delivery times to under 2 hours in 70% of NA orders, improving Net Promoter Scores to 72. We've also rolled out headless CMS for seamless buy-online-pickup-in-store integration with retailers like Whole Foods and Albertsons, blending e-com with our 65% traditional retail base.

Strategically, e-commerce isn't just a growth engine—it's enhancing our gross margins by 320 basis points to 42% in the channel, thanks to lower slotting fees versus CPG trade spend and direct customer data for R&D. Unlike slower incumbents like General Mills, where e-com is still sub-10% of revenues, we're leveraging first-party data from 12 million active users to forecast demand for trending categories like functional foods, which grew 60% in our portfolio. Sustainability plays a role too: our recyclable e-com packaging, certified by How2Recycle, resonates with 45% of Gen Z shoppers per our surveys, driving repeat purchases.

Looking forward, we expect e-commerce to contribute 22-24% of total revenues by FY2025, with mid-40s year-over-year growth in 2024, contingent on moderating freight costs and consumer confidence. Risks include rising parcel rates—up 8% industry-wide—and competitive intensity from private labels like Amazon's Wicked Kitchen plant-based line. But with our $150 million capex plan for AI-driven personalization and international expansion, we're well-positioned to sustain this momentum.

Next, on the impact of new product innovations and launches, which has been a cornerstone of our growth strategy, especially as consumer preferences shift toward health, sustainability, and convenience. In Q3, our new product portfolio—defined as launches within the last 24 months—delivered $1.2 billion in net revenue, representing 18% of our total Food & Beverage segment sales and a robust 32% year-over-year growth. That's outpacing our overall segment growth of 12% and the broader industry average of just 8%, per NielsenIQ data. This isn't just top-line momentum; these innovations are accretive to margins, contributing 450 basis points to our segment gross margin expansion, now at 42.5%. Premiumization plays a big role—our new SKUs command 15-20% pricing premiums over legacy products, driven by clean-label formulations and functional benefits that resonate with millennials and Gen Z, who now account for 62% of our household penetration in key markets, up from 55% last year.

Breaking it down by category, our plant-based and functional beverage platforms were the stars. Our VitaBloom line of adaptogen-infused ready-to-drink teas, launched in Q1, hit $450 million in Q3 sales, a staggering 150% year-over-year increase, fueled by viral TikTok campaigns and partnerships with influencers in the wellness space. IRI scan data shows VitaBloom achieving top-decile velocity in the $4.99 price tier, with repeat purchase rates at 28% within the first 90 days—well above the category norm of 18%. We're leveraging precision fermentation tech here, partnering with biotech leaders like Perfect Day and Ginkgo Bioworks, to create dairy-free creamers with mouthfeel rivaling traditional half-and-half. This tech reduced our ingredient costs by 12% while enabling complete protein claims that align with the high-protein trend exploding across F&B.

On the snack side, our EarthCrunch sustainable protein bars—made with upcycled cricket flour and regenerative agriculture-sourced nuts—ramped to $320 million in Q3 revenue, up 45% year-over-year. These launched in Europe mid-year and quickly captured 2.1% market share in the €2-3 billion protein bar segment, per Euromonitor. Gross margins here are elite at 48%, thanks to localized sourcing that cuts logistics costs by 15% and our proprietary extrusion tech for extended shelf life without preservatives. Sustainability is table stakes now; 78% of consumers in our Kantar surveys cite it as a purchase driver, and EarthCrunch boasts B Corp certification with 90% recyclable packaging, putting us ahead of competitors like Mondelez's RXBAR or Clif Bar.

Regionally, North America drove 55% of new product sales or $660 million, riding the plant-based wave. VitaBloom expanded to 85% ACV in the U.S., with double-digit distribution gains at key retailers like Whole Foods and Kroger. Household penetration jumped 8 points to 22%, outpacing category leader Celsius by 3 points. Inflationary pressures have helped—consumers trading up to our $3.49 multipacks amid +7% CPG inflation. Europe contributed $380 million or 32%, where regulatory tailwinds like the EU's Farm-to-Fork strategy favor our clean-label creds. EarthCrunch saw +25% year-over-year growth in the UK and Germany, grabbing share from Nestlé's plant-based offerings. We navigated aspartame scrutiny by reformulating our low-cal RTDs to stevia-monk fruit blends ahead of the curve, boosting velocities by 15%.

In Asia-Pacific, our fastest-growing region at +55% year-over-year for new products or $160 million, we're tailoring to local tastes. ZenFuel kombucha sodas, launched in Japan and Indonesia, leverage co-fermentation with yuzu and matcha for functional gut health claims. These hit 12% market share in the ¥500 billion RTD tea market within six months, partnering with 7-Eleven for exclusive vending. APAC's urbanization trend—projected 60% urban by 2030 per McKinsey—drives impulse buys, and our lightweight, resealable pouches have lifted impulse sales by 22%. Emerging markets like LATAM and MEA added $60 million, with affordable innovations like value-pack plantain chips under our TropiFuel brand. These grew 40% year-over-year, capturing low-income consumers amid +10% food inflation, with SKU rationalization ensuring 95% in-stock rates.

Strategically, these launches underscore our Innovate-to-Lead framework: $250 million invested in R&D this year, up 20% year-over-year, focusing on three pillars—biotech for novel ingredients, AI-driven flavor modeling via our SensoryAI platform, reducing development time by 30%, and circular economy packaging with suppliers like Amcor. We've filed 12 new patents in fermentation and upcycling, positioning us to defend against private label encroachment, which now claims 28% of F&B shelves per IRI. Pipeline-wise, Q4 brings HydroPure electrolyte waters with NAD+ boosters—targeting the $15 billion functional water space—and FlexiMeat hybrid burgers blending mycelium and pea protein, aiming for $800 million run-rate by FY25. We're eyeing M&A too, like bolt-ons in precision ag to secure supply chains amid climate volatility. Risks include supply chain snarls from Red Sea disruptions, a 2% headwind, but our dual-sourcing mitigated it. Competitively, PepsiCo's Poppi acquisition and Unilever's growing functionals keep us sharp—we're +500 bps ahead on new product NPS scores. In sum, new innovations are driving 2 points of organic growth this year and reshaping our portfolio for mid-teens expansion. We expect them to contribute 20-22% of FY24 revenue, with margins expanding another 100-150 bps.

Turning to our revised or reaffirmed full-year guidance, which we are today reaffirming at the top end of our prior ranges, with a slight upward revision to adjusted diluted EPS to reflect the momentum across our core categories. This reaffirmation underscores the strength of our diversified portfolio, disciplined pricing execution, and early payoffs from supply chain resilience initiatives amid a still-challenging macroeconomic backdrop. Back in our Q2 call, we guided for full-year organic net sales growth of 4% to 6%, adjusted EBITDA margins of 18.5% to 19.5%, and adjusted diluted EPS of $4.40 to $4.60. Today, based on Q3 results—which delivered 7.2% organic sales growth, up from 5.8% in Q2—we are reaffirming organic net sales growth at 5% to 6%, implying a full-year top-end bias toward 6%. We're also reaffirming adjusted EBITDA margins at 19% to 19.5%, benefiting from 250 basis points of gross margin expansion year-over-year in Q3 alone, driven by targeted pricing actions averaging 8% across our portfolio and productivity savings from our Nourish Forward cost transformation program. Most notably, we are revising adjusted diluted EPS guidance upward to $4.55 to $4.70, from the prior range. This $0.15 increase at the midpoint reflects stronger-than-expected volume performance in our high-margin Health & Wellness segment, which grew 12% organically in Q3, and $150 million in incremental free cash flow from working capital efficiencies. We continue to expect full-year capex at 3.5% of sales, or approximately $650 million, weighted toward high-ROI automation projects like our new aseptic filling lines in Mexico and AI-driven demand sensing platforms across North American beverage plants.

Sales dynamics show our 5% to 6% organic growth outlook holds despite consumer value-seeking, as Nielsen data shows 2% category contraction in at-home snacks through October. We're outpacing through premiumization: 60% of incremental Q3 sales from higher-margin SKUs like Nourish Protein Bars—now #3 in the $2.5 billion U.S. protein bar category—and Zero Sugar Energy Drinks, gaining 1.5 share points versus Monster and Red Bull. Pricing remains a tailwind at 4% to 5% for the year, while volumes track +1% overall, with away-from-home up 4%. Segment-wise, Beverages at 45% of sales on track for 6% growth, fueled by RTD coffee expansions like Starbucks Nitro Cold Brew partnership, up 25% volumes in Europe, and plant-based alternatives amid 15% category surge per Euromonitor. Snacks & Confectionery at 30% reaffirms 4%, with savory like Kettle Harvest Potato Chips holding share. Health & Wellness at 15% pacing 11-12%, driven by Greek Probiotic yogurt now 20% of $8 billion U.S. spoonable market. Legacy Dairy & Ingredients flat to +1%, stabilized via forward contracts covering 85% of 2025 milk needs.

Regionally, Americas at 65% of sales guiding to 7% growth, with U.S. +2% volumes on 10% share gains in healthier snacks. Mexico and Brazil double-digit via local production. Europe at 20% for 3% growth despite energy costs 15% above 2023, via exports and plant-based uplift. APAC/EM at 15% for 8%, China RTD tea +15%, India snacking +20%. Margins benefit from pricing, supply chain optimization, mix shift. Input costs inflecting, hedged 70% of 2025 commodities for $200 million savings. Nourish Forward delivered $120 million Q3 savings via 15% network consolidation and robotic palletizing cutting labor 20%. SAP S/4HANA cut inventory to 45 days. Post $1.2 billion PlantPower acquisition, 25% beverage sales plant-based. Divestitures generated $300 million for buybacks. Sustainability: Scope 3 down 12% via regenerative ag on 50,000 acres. Risks: tariffs 50 bps COGS, FX $0.05 EPS drag. Balance sheet net debt/EBITDA 2.1x, $1.5 billion liquidity, 45-50% payout.

Now, on the impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue, a key headwind we've navigated. With 48% of our $12.4 billion trailing twelve-month revenue from international markets via brands like ZestQuench soft drinks, CrunchWave snacks, NutriPure dairy alternatives, this exposure drives growth but brings FX sensitivity. Q3 revenue $3.1 billion reported up 4%, but constant currency 7.2%. FX dragged 320 basis points or $98 million, from stronger USD—dollar index up 5.8% QoQ. Similar to Nestlé's 2-3% hit. Europe 22% revenue: $45 million drag from EUR/USD -4.2%, masking 6% volume in carbonated soft drinks; pricing offset 60%. APAC 15%: $32 million, JPY -7.1%, IDR/PHP -5-6%; snacks +9% ex-FX. LATAM 8%: $15 million from BRL/MXN -4-5%; dairy +12% volumes. Other EM $6 million. YTD FX shaved 2.4 points, TTM $285 million hit, but organic constant currency 6.8%. Hedging now 75% 2025 exposure, up from 55%; transactional 90%. Localizing 65% APAC sourcing. Q4 neutral to 1% headwind; pricing +4-5% counters. Long-term, India/SE Asia to 20% revenue by 2027.

Shifting to EBITDA margin performance and key factors, a standout at 17.8%, up 140 basis points year-over-year, strongest in two years, ahead of guidance. TTM 16.9% from 15.2%. Gross margin up 210 bps to 38.4% from 6.2% pricing, esp. ZestEnergy, PureHarvest. Commodity basket down 8% QoQ; cocoa to $7,200, hedged 70% FY24 at 15% below spot. $45 million gross savings or 120 bps from precision ag cutting grains 12%, AI demand sensing cutting inventory 18%, service 98.5%. SG&A down 70 bps to 12.1% via ZBB, 5% headcount cut, digital marketing ROI +25%. NA 65% sales: 19.2% margin +180 bps on premium shift, e-com 15%. EMEA 20%: 14.5% resilient vs deflation. APAC/LATAM 15%: +221 bps to 21.3% on RTD teas. Headwinds: FX 20 bps, freight 10 bps. FY24 guide 16.5-17.5% or $1.25-1.30B EBITDA. Divesting dairy plants $150M for innovation. Scope 3 down 12%.

Regarding organic revenue growth overall and by region, we hit 6.8% year-over-year constant currency, exceeding midpoint, third quarter accelerating. +4.2% price/mix from 85% SKUs, premiumization like VitaPure, GreenHarvest +22%. Volume +2.6% from e-com/club. NA 47% revenue +8.2%: price/mix +5.1%, volume +3.1% foodservice. EMEA 28% +5.1%: price/mix +3.4%, Eastern +9.4%. APAC 18% +7.9%: China +11.5%, India +8.7%. LATAM 7% +4.3% ex-FX +9.2%. FY24 5-7% via portfolio elevation, execution, sustainability.

On performance in key channels: retail, foodservice, convenience, driving 8.2% organic growth vs industry 4.1%. Retail 52% +7.5%: volume +2.1%, price/mix +5.4%; grocery +1.8 pts penetration, club/e-com +14%/22%. Foodservice 28% +10.3%: volume +4.2%, QSR partnerships +25%. Convenience 20% +9.8%: velocity +11%, impulse 65%+. Mix shift favorable, margins +120 bps.

Finally, performance of key brands and product categories: Consumer Brands 72% revenues +8.2% organic, op income +12.1%, margins +110 bps to 22.4%. Beverages 42% +11.7%: Quench +0.8 pts share, VitaBoost +28%. Snacking 31% +6.1%: SnapCrunch +7.2%, PeakNut +19%. Health/Convenience 27% +14.3%: GreenHarvest +32%. NA +9.8%, EMEA +7.5%, APAC/LATAM +6.2%. SKU prune funds innovations; M&A eyed.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Mike Rivera (CEO):
Thanks, John. Inflation remains a headwind across inputs like cocoa, dairy, and freight, up mid-teens in spots, but we've offset it effectively with 6-8% pricing across the portfolio, leveraging brand strength in premium health categories where elasticity is low. Our hedging covers 70% of key commodities, and productivity from Nourish Forward saved $120 million in Q3 alone. Volumes held up in away-from-home channels, and premium mix shift added 200 bps to gross margins. We're gaining share versus peers facing similar pressures, positioning us well.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Emily Carter (JPMorgan):
What are your plans for VitaBloom and what is the expected impact of the product?

Lisa Chen (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Emily. VitaBloom adaptogen RTD teas, launched Q1, are ramping beautifully at $450 million Q3 sales, +150% year-over-year, with top-decile velocity and 28% repeat rates. Plans include further distribution to 90% ACV, new flavors via precision fermentation, and APAC expansion. We expect $800 million run-rate FY24, contributing 2 points to organic growth and 450 bps to margins through 15-20% premiums, aligning with health trends outpacing category leaders.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

David Lee (Morgan Stanley):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Tom Bradley (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Thanks, David. Disruptions like Red Sea rerouting and avian flu have been challenging, creating 2% headwinds, but our dual-sourcing across 65% of inputs, localized production in key regions like Brazil and Mexico, and AI forecasting have kept service levels at 98.5%. We've consolidated networks 15%, invested in micro-fulfillment, and hedged commodities, delivering $45 million savings. Multi-modal logistics 60% rail/sea limits freight risks, ensuring 95% in-stock for innovations.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Rachel Kim with Barclays. Please proceed.

Rachel Kim (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Sarah Jenkins (CFO):
Thanks, Rachel. Q4 outlook remains strong, with organic growth biased to 6-7%, led by foodservice +10%, e-com mid-40s, new products 20% of sales. EBITDA margins 19-19.5%, EPS top end $4.70, assuming stable FX and moderating inputs. Tailwinds from premiumization, innovations like HydroPure, channel shifts; risks like tariffs or FX offset by pricing +4-5%, hedging. Confident in mid-single-digit FY24 delivery, outpacing peers.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Mike Rivera for closing remarks.

Mike Rivera (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in NutriFresh Foods Inc. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
